items.title: Sub-Part 9: Unstained as Space, Unshaken as Indra's Banner

items.zh: 智者如空無染污，不動猶如天帝幢；如泛清涼盈滿池，不樂淤泥生死海。
items.en: The wise one is like space, unstained; unshaken, like the banner of the god of the devas; drifting as though on a cool, brimming pool, taking no pleasure in the muddy sea of birth-and-death.

items.zh: 今此頌中，辯阿羅漢苾芻心善解脫，超諸戲論，猶如虛空。何以故？譬如虛空離諸戲論，淨與不淨皆不能染。諸阿羅漢亦復如是，一切世法若順、若違皆不能染。所謂利、衰，乃至苦、樂。又諸有學已離欲貪，向阿羅漢，於四念住善住其心，修無相心三摩地時，如天帝幢；於其一切動發憍舉、戲論營為、生願俱行所有貪愛，不能傾動。又諸有學已離欲貪，得不還果，於上解脫心生欲樂。譬如遊泛清冷泉池，於愛味定上分諸結熱淤泥中，終不欣樂。由於此中不欣樂故，亦不欣樂生死大海。復有差別。謂阿羅漢所有飲食、言說、遊行，處無相住，有餘依苦之所隨逐。如其次第，三處應知。復有差別。謂慧解脫諸阿羅漢、有學身證，及俱解脫諸阿羅漢。如其次第，三處應知。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，離三界欲於佛聖旨猶有餘依，離欲界貪勝進道攝，及不還果。復有差別。謂略顯示解脫勝利、等持勝利、智慧勝利。復有差別。謂略顯示增上心、慧學所得果。及顯增上心、慧二學。

items.title: Sub-Part 10: Seeing the Buddha's Form Is Not the Same as Knowing the Buddha

items.zh: 若以色量我，以音聲尋我；欲貪所執持，彼不能知我。若於內了知，於外不能見；由內果觀察，彼音聲所引。若於內無知，於外而能見；由外果觀察，亦音聲所引。若於內無知，於外不能見；彼普障愚夫，亦音聲所引。若於內了知，於外亦能見；英雄出離慧，非音聲所引。
items.en: If one measures me by form, or seeks me by sound — held fast by desire and craving, such a one cannot know me. If one knows within but cannot see without, seeing only through the fruit of inner meditation, such a one is still led by mere sound. If one has no knowledge within yet can see without, seeing only through the fruit of outer sense, such a one is still led by mere sound. If one has no knowledge within and cannot see without, wholly obstructed and confused, such a one too is led by mere sound. But if one knows within and also sees without — the hero possessed of the wisdom of renunciation — such a one is not led by mere sound.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂如有一，體是異生，未斷虛妄分別欲貪，觀見世尊具三十二大丈夫相，遂便測量：此薄伽梵，定是如來應正等覺，其所說法決定微妙，其弟子眾所行必善。彼於後時，近不善人，聞不正法，隨逐他論及他音聲，信順於他，他所引攝；他所引故，於佛法僧還生毀謗。如是皆由不如實知如來法身，故致如此。復有異生，由內靜慮果天眼通，遠見世尊，便作是解：此薄伽梵，定是如來應正等覺。餘如前說。復有由外欲界繫業果報肉眼，見已測量；當知彼亦隨逐他論及他音聲，信順於他，他所引攝。復有異生，於爾所見都無所有；彼普被障，長時為他音聲所引。若諸賢聖，除斷、調伏、超越欲貪，得聖慧眼。彼由如是聖慧眼故，於內證解如來法身。雖於外見如來色身，或見制多，或圖畫等，而能了知非第一義應正等覺。彼由如是於內正知，於外正觀，不隨他論及他音聲，不信順他，非他所引，於佛法僧決定信受。如是皆由如實了知如來法身，故致如此。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，若唯世俗見如來者，則不決定；若以勝義見如來者，是則決定。當知是名此中略義。

blocks.text: Two verses. The second will remind many readers of a famous line in the *Diamond Sūtra*. The explanations are **untranslated**; the commentary summarises them.

subs.head: Like space, like a banner, like a cool pool

blocks.text: "The wise one is like space, unstained; unshaken, like the banner of the lord of the gods; drifting as though on a cool, brimming pool, taking no pleasure in the muddy sea of birth and death."

The prose (untranslated): **like space**, the arhat's liberated mind is beyond proliferation, and no worldly condition, gain or loss, praise or blame, pain or pleasure, can stain it. Master Cháng Bǎi: these are the eight worldly winds. **Like Indra's banner**, a trainee free of sense desire and practising the signless concentration is not moved by craving. **Like one floating on a cool pool**, the non-returner does not relish the "hot mud" of attachment to meditation, and so does not delight in saṃsāra.
"If one measures me by form, or seeks me by sound, held fast by desire, such a one cannot know me."

The prose (untranslated) describes four kinds of people: - An ordinary person sees the Buddha's thirty-two marks and concludes, "He must be the Buddha; his Dharma must be sublime." Later, meeting bad teachers, the same person follows their words and slanders the Three Jewels, because they never knew the **Dharma body** (法身). - Another sees the Buddha from afar with the divine eye of meditation, and draws the same conclusion; Venerable Miào Jìng: the divine eye also sees only outer appearances. - Another sees with ordinary eyes and is likewise led by others. - Another sees nothing at all, and is entirely led by others' words.

But the noble ones, with the eye of noble wisdom, know the Dharma body inwardly. Even when they see the Buddha's form, or a stūpa, or a painting, they know this is not the Buddha in the ultimate sense; their faith is unshakeable.

In brief: to see the Buddha only conventionally is unreliable; to see him in the ultimate sense is certain. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha is called Buddha because he realised the suchness of all things, not because of the thirty-two marks.

quiz.q: How does the ninth verse describe the wise one?
options: unstained like space, unshaken like the banner of the lord of the gods, drifting as on a cool full pool, taking no pleasure in the muddy sea of birth and death
quiz.why: "The wise one is like space, unstained; unshaken, like the banner of the god of the devas; drifting as though on a cool, brimming pool, taking no pleasure in the muddy sea of birth-and-death." Venerable Miào Jìng: this wise one is the arhat.

quiz.q: In "unshaken, like the banner of the lord of the gods," what does "unshaken" mean, per the two masters?
options: Cháng Bǎi: unmoved by the eight worldly winds, like Śakra's banner; Miào Jìng: neither leaning nor shaking
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not shaken by the eight worldly winds — gain, loss, defamation, fame, praise, ridicule, pain, and pleasure — like the banner of Śakra, lord of the gods. Venerable Miào Jìng: "leaning" is the mind tilting, "moving" is shaking; like the lord of the gods' banner, it neither leans nor shakes.

quiz.q: Who is the "wise one" of the verse, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the arhat — the noble monk whose mind has achieved fine liberation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this wise one is the arhat, a person of wisdom; this noble monk's mind has already achieved fine liberation.

quiz.q: According to the first verse, who "cannot know me"?
options: those who never saw the Buddha
those who measure me by form, seek me by sound, and are held fast by desire and craving
quiz.why: "If one measures me by form, or seeks me by sound — held fast by desire and craving, such a one cannot know me." Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha is called Buddha for realising the suchness of phenomena, not for the thirty-two marks.

quiz.q: Why, per Venerable Miào Jìng, is the Buddha called "Buddha"?
options: for realising the suchness of phenomena, not for the thirty-two marks
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha is called Buddha because he realised the suchness of all phenomena — not because of the thirty-two marks.

quiz.q: Who is the one who "has no knowledge within and cannot see without," per the two masters?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the blind who cannot see even in the Buddha's time, and ordinary beings after his passing; Miào Jìng: only the blind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one kind is blind — though born in the Buddha's time, he cannot see with physical eyes; another is the ordinary person after the Buddha's passing. Venerable Miào Jìng: he has no divine eye and has also lost his physical sight — such a person should be called blind.

quiz.q: Someone who sees the Buddha's marks with the divine eye — whom, per Venerable Miào Jìng, are they really no different from?
options: an ordinary person with physical eyes — still discriminating outer appearances, lacking noble wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the divine eye also discriminates outer appearances; such a person has not attained noble wisdom, and so is in substance the same as an ordinary person with physical eyes — still "led by mere sound."
